Build a TreePPL sampler for a given model and inference method

Source: R/model.R
tp_sampler.Rd

tp_sampler() compiles a TreePPL model with the chosen inference method and returns a sampler that can be run with tp_run(). The model is compiled once; the sampler can then be run many times, with different data or runtime options, without compiling again.

Usage

tp_sampler(model, method = "mcmc", print = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

model

One of three options:

  • the path to a .tppl file with the TreePPL code, OR

  • the name of a model in the TreePPL model library (see tp_model_library()), e.g. "crbd", OR

  • a string containing the entire TreePPL code.

These are tried in this order: an existing file first, then a library model, and otherwise the string is treated as code.

method

Inference method to compile the model with. See tp_treeppl_options("methods") for all supported methods.

print

Whether to print information about the sampler when it is created.

...

Compile options, as name = value pairs or a single list (see tp_list()). See tp_treeppl_options("compile") for all supported options. Names are written without --, and underscores are converted to hyphens (e.g., incremental_printing = TRUE becomes --incremental-printing). Runtime options are not allowed here; pass them to tp_run() instead.

Value

Invisibly, a list of class tpSampler with elements:

  • exe_path: path to the compiled sampler executable.

  • model_path: path to the .tppl file that was compiled.

  • method: the inference method.

  • compile_opt: the compile options used, as a named list.

See also

tp_run() to run the sampler, tp_list() to collect options, tp_treeppl_options() for the available methods and options.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Library model, SMC with aligned resampling and pruning
sampler <- tp_sampler(
  model = "crbd",
  method = "smc-bpf",
  resample = "align",
  prune = TRUE
)

# Your own model file, default method (MCMC)
sampler <- tp_sampler(model = "path/to/my_model.tppl")
} # }
